newsitem.title: BRAZIL: African nations seek cut in ACPC exports - minister.
newsitem.headline: African nations seek cut in ACPC exports - minister.

text.p: African coffee producing members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) are seeking a 2.5 million bag cut in member exports between January and June 1997, said Uganda's Trade and Industry Minister.
"We are looking at a cut of one million bags in robusta and 1.5 million bags in arabica," Abel Rwendeire told Reuters.
Rwendeire declined to say what role major robusta producer Indonesia would play in any reduction.
But he added that African officials would be meeting Indonesian officials in Rio de Janeiro on January 22 ahead of an emergency meeting of the ACPC on January 23.
On the arabica side, Rwendeire said that Colombia had indicated in a meeting in December that it would be prepared to reduce its exports in January to June 1997 by around 300,000 bags.
Under a plan to be put to ACPC members this week, Brazil would take the largest cut of all arabica producers.
Rwendeire said Vietnam, currently not an ACPC member, has also indicated that it would informally participate in any effort to regulate exports in the first half of the year.
"They said that they could retain coffee and release it later in May when there is not a lot of coffee available from other suppliers," he said.
In meetings last week with Vietnamese government and export officials, an African delegation had been told that the Vietnamese could slow their exports in February, March and April, Rwendeire said.
Under the ACPC export plan, African nations should export no more than 6.52 million bags but in reality it is unlikely to be able to meet that quota, Rwendeire said.
"Cutting exports is not a problem. Given anticipation of production, we will not be able to reach what we were expected to export," Rwendeire said.
